elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
Transition assistance charged at then-current rates
Return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format
elements.evidence: "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" — machine-readable is express, but "commonly used" is not stated as a standard format

elements.element: Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry or termination (mandatory, not request-gated)
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Customer Data" — the 30-day clock runs from a Customer request, not from expiry or termination

elements.element: Deletion of Customer Data after return
elements.evidence: "thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems"

elements.element: Data export within 30 days of termination
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Customer's request" — export duty is triggered only by a request rather than by expiry or termination

reasons: The inserted 10.3(b) ties the 30-day data-return clock to "Customer's request" rather than to expiry or termination, so the mandatory post-termination return obligation is request-gated; if no request is made, no data is returned and the downstream deletion/certification mechanic in (c) never starts.
Fix: change (b) to "within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination" (a short phrase edit suffices), which restores both the preferred and fallback data-return element.

The format wording says "commonly used, machine-readable format" rather than the playbook's standard machine-readable format; machine-readability is express, but the standard-format element is not clearly stated.
Transition assistance elements (six months, then-current rates) and the deletion/written-certification sequence are all expressly met.

The insertion is a concise new clause for an otherwise absent obligation and does not disturb 10.1, 10.2 or 16.5, so minimality and intent are preserved; the "subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements" carve-out mirrors existing 16.5 and could be dropped as duplicative.
